subject.title: [Feature]: Bedrock provider should support guardrail input tagging (guardContent) so Prompt-attack filter doesn't false-block on the system prompt

question: Should the Amazon Bedrock plugin retain all-request guardrail evaluation as the default and add an explicit selective-input mode, or should configured guardrails switch to selective evaluation by default?
rationale: The current shipped feature intentionally applies configured guardrails to every Bedrock invocation, while selective evaluation changes what security controls inspect. Source and AWS contracts establish that both modes are possible, but they cannot determine the intended operator-safe default or the trust classification for injected and tool-derived content.

options.title: Add opt-in selective mode
options.body: Preserve current all-request evaluation by default and add a documented provider setting that tags only an explicitly defined set of untrusted content.

options.title: Make selective evaluation the default
options.body: Change configured guardrails to exclude trusted system content by default, with an explicit all-request mode for operators who need the previous coverage.

options.title: Keep all-request behavior
options.body: Retain the existing configuration contract and address only guardrail-intervention diagnostics in the related issue.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in selective mode
recommendation.body: Preserve current all-request evaluation by default and add a documented provider setting that tags only an explicitly defined set of untrusted content.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and approved the original feature whose all-request semantics this decision would preserve or revise.
